To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pattern of intrinsic disorder within Myc transcription factors may be a more conserved property than the amino acid sequence and that this pattern can be used as an alternative approach to making dendograms of Myc proteins to aid classification of the proteins.
the pattern of protein disorder along the sequence of Myc proteins is highly conserved and that this pattern can be used to make phylogenetic relationships between Myc proteins.

the pattern of intrinsic disorder within the Myc proteins can aid the classification of Mycs, including Myc-like proteins, and that the N-terminal domain of Myc proteins has been conserved to a much greater degree than previously appreciated.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Myc proteins have evolved from a simple ancestral protein with high levels of intrinsic protein disorder and that the pattern of protein disorder has been maintained through evolution.
intrinsic protein disorder is an important feature of Myc proteins, which has been conserved through evolution, but that the pattern of amino acid sequence conservation is not as strong.
intrinsic protein disorder is a conserved feature of the Myc family of proteins and that this can be used to trace the origins of the Myc proteins to simpler eukaryotic organisms.
